governing_document.reason: 2025-18469 is the final rule (Amendment 39-23153, AD 2025-19-13). No correction was published in the thread, so its regulatory text controls over the proposed rule 2025-10764.

eligible_parts.description: A part eligible for installation is an HPT 1st-stage hub or HPT 2nd-stage hub having a P/N and S/N that is not listed in table 1 to paragraph (g). The definition names no eligible part numbers. It excludes only the specific P/N and S/N combinations in table 1.

required_actions.description: For engines with an installed part (P/N and S/N) identified in table 1 to paragraph (g): at the next engine shop visit after the effective date, before exceeding the applicable removal cycle limit in table 1 or within 100 flight cycles from the effective date, whichever occurs later, remove the affected part from service and replace it with a part eligible for installation.

installation_prohibitions.description: After the effective date, do not install in any engine an HPT 1st-stage hub or HPT 2nd-stage hub that has a P/N and S/N listed in table 1 to paragraph (g).

ambiguities.description: The sentence joins three timing elements: the next engine shop visit after the effective date, 'before exceeding the applicable removal cycle limit', and 'within 100 flight cycles from the effective date'. These are followed by 'whichever occurs later'. The text does not settle whether the shop visit is one of the alternatives being compared, or how the shop visit relates to the two cycle limits. This changes when removal is due.
readings: Remove at the next engine shop visit after the effective date, but no later than the later of (a) reaching the table 1 removal cycle limit (cycles since new) and (b) 100 flight cycles after the effective date. Whichever comes first, the shop visit or that backstop, triggers removal.

The deadline is the later of (a) reaching the table 1 removal cycle limit and (b) 100 flight cycles after the effective date. The shop visit only describes where the work is expected to be done, not an earlier trigger.

Removal is required at the next engine shop visit only if that shop visit occurs before the part exceeds its table 1 removal cycle limit. Otherwise removal is due within 100 flight cycles after the effective date. 'Whichever occurs later' compares the shop-visit-before-limit timing with the 100 flight cycle timing.

ambiguities.description: The engine shop visit definition refers to 'separation of any major mating engine flanges, H-P' without saying what 'H-P' means. This affects which maintenance events count as an engine shop visit, and so when paragraph (g) is triggered.
readings: Separation of any major mating flange in the range of flange designations H through P.
Separation of the flanges designated H and P only.

notes: No correction documents are in the thread. The final rule's regulatory text matches the proposed rule (2025-10764) except that paragraph (a) changed from 'Comments Due Date' to 'Effective Date'. The final rule states it was adopted as proposed except for minor editorial changes.

Applicability under paragraph (c) covers all listed engine models regardless of installed parts. The FAA declined a comment asking to limit applicability to engines with the affected hubs, so that the paragraph (h) installation prohibition applies to all listed models.
Table 1 is titled 'Affected HPT 1st Stage and HPT 2nd Stage Hubs'. Its removal cycle limits are stated in cycles since new.

HPT 1st-stage hub S/N PKLBSK9287 has a removal cycle limit of only 100 cycles since new. This hub may already be past its limit, which makes the 100 flight cycles from the effective date timing especially relevant to this part.

Paragraph (g) acts on parts identified by both P/N and S/N. A screening program should match the P/N and S/N combination, not the P/N alone, since part numbers 2A5001 and 2A4802 are not affected by themselves.
Paragraph (l) states that no material is incorporated by reference.
